Working notes — Days 1–10

- Daily setup: send window is 10am. Choose one angle: A price cut, B quality story, C limited-time urgency, D customer testimonial. Legal has signed off on all four.
- Context: Day 1 unsubscribes were processed. No deliverability complaints on Days 3 and 10. List grew by a few signups on several days.
- Angles used: B, C, D, C, C, D, C, D, D, B. Angle A has not been tested.
- Outcomes: each day’s report only said “Push queued” (+0.00), which is not actual performance. Final aggregate: 6 of the last 10 pushes landed. No per-day or per-angle breakdown is available, so we cannot attribute results to any angle.
- Decision guidance:
  - Treat +0.00 as “queued/no result yet,” not failure.
  - Trust the aggregate: 60% landed over 10 pushes. Keep cadence and watch aggregate reports.
  - Do not overfit to angle choices without attribution. C/D were most frequent, B less, A never used.
  - Consider testing A next if useful, but do not assume it will outperform. Legal cleared it.
  - Continue rotating B/C/D for balance if no per-angle data. Keep 10am window, process unsubscribes promptly, monitor deliverability.
- Open need: request per-day/per-angle analytics to optimize future angle selection.

Working notes — Days 1–20

- Daily setup: 10am send window. Choose one angle: A price cut, B quality story, C limited-time urgency, D customer testimonial. Legal cleared all four.
- Operations: process unsubscribes promptly; monitor deliverability. No deliverability complaints on most checked days. List has grown by small signups.
- Angle history: Days 1–10: B,C,D,C,C,D,C,D,D,B. Days 11–20: A,B,A,A,B,A,A,A,A,A. Totals: A8, B4, C4, D4. A was untested before Day11; now A is the most-used angle.
- Outcomes: Daily +0.00 means “Push queued,” not failure or final result. Day20 aggregate: 7 of last 10 pushes landed. No per-day or per-angle breakdown, so angle performance cannot be attributed.
- Decision guidance:
  - Trust aggregate only: 70% of last 10 landed. Keep cadence and watch aggregate reports.
  - Do not infer A is better despite recent heavy use; no per-angle evidence.
  - +0.00 is not a failed send.
  - Avoid overfitting to C/D or A. If no attribution, rotate angles for balance. A is now over-indexed; consider B/C/D next unless there is a testing rationale.
  - Keep 10am window, process unsubscribes promptly, monitor deliverability.
- Open need: request per-day/per-angle analytics (landed, opens/clicks/unsubs if available) to optimize angle choice.

Working notes — Days 1–30

- Daily setup: 10am send window. Choose one angle: A price cut, B quality story, C limited-time urgency, D customer testimonial. Legal cleared all four. Design refreshed banner art on Day25.
- Ops: process unsubscribes promptly; monitor deliverability. No complaints most checked mornings. List grew by small signups.
- Angle history: Days1–10: B,C,D,C,C,D,C,D,D,B. Days11–20: A,B,A,A,B,A,A,A,A,A. Days21–30: C x10. Totals: A8, B4, C14, D4. C is now heavily over-indexed; A was over-indexed earlier.
- Outcomes: +0.00 means “Push queued,” not failure/final result. Day20 aggregate: 7/10 last pushes landed. Day30 aggregate: 4/10 last pushes landed. No per-day/per-angle breakdown, but our send log shows the last 10 pushes were all C, so the recent C-only streak coincides with a lower aggregate landed rate. Small sample: avoid overclaiming, but stop defaulting to C.
- Decision guidance:
  - Keep 10am window, prompt unsubscribes, deliverability watch.
  - Do not treat +0.00 as a failed send.
  - Stop the C streak. Rotate to B or D (least used), then A if needed; do not assume A is superior.
  - Trust aggregate reports; watch whether landed rate recovers after rotating.
  - Request per-day/per-angle analytics (landed, opens/clicks/unsubs) to confirm attribution. Open need remains.
